subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should maintainers sponsor a focused current-main or packaged repro pass for #87980 before allowing an automated fix PR?
rationale: The report is concrete, but source inspection only proves normal exec should preserve command text; it does not prove which current path, if any, still mutates redirects.

options.title: Reproduce before fix
options.body: Run a focused packaged/current-main exec scenario and queue implementation only after the mutation boundary is identified.

options.title: Wait for reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but require fresh logs, terminal output, or a recording before maintainer engineering time is spent.

options.title: Close after non-repro proof
options.body: If maintainers prove current main and the latest package preserve `2>&1` and `2>/dev/null`, close with that exact proof.

recommendation.title: Reproduce before fix
recommendation.body: Run a focused packaged/current-main exec scenario and queue implementation only after the mutation boundary is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the deepest local history across the exec runtime and redirect-adjacent approval/allowlist code.
